parsed.summary: The Lean statement is Cauchy's theorem. For a finite group G (with a Fintype instance) and a prime p dividing |G|, there exists x in G with orderOf x = p. It matches the paper exactly. No substantive caveat: Fintype.card is the true cardinality, and a group is nonempty, so the card-zero junk value does not arise.

glossary.plain: the order |G| of the finite group G
the order of the element x (0 if infinite order; it cannot be infinite in a finite group)

lean_claims.plain: For every finite group G and every prime p with p dividing |G|, there exists x in G whose order is exactly p.

paper_claims.plain: If G is a finite group and p is a prime dividing |G|, then G contains an element of order p.

coverage.why: The hypotheses and conclusion correspond directly.

lint_verdicts.why: G is a group, so it is nonempty (it contains 1), hence Fintype.card G ≥ 1 and the zero junk value is impossible. Fintype also guarantees finiteness.
